title: Make Array Non-decreasing
summary: Given an integer array, you can perform operations to replace a subarray with its maximum value.
statement: Given an integer array, you can perform operations to replace a subarray with its maximum value. The goal is to make the array non-decreasing with the largest possible array size after zero or more operations.
constraints: nums has up to 200,000 positive integers.
An operation replaces any nonempty contiguous subarray by its maximum value.
After any operations, maximize the length of a non-decreasing resulting array.
hints: A retained block contributes its maximum, and the next block must end at a value at least that maximum.
Scan left to right, retaining exactly the values that meet the largest maximum forced so far.
Increment the answer when value >= current maximum, then set the current maximum to that value.
Any skipped values can be absorbed into the next retained block; taking the earliest feasible endpoint leaves maximal room for later blocks.
editorial: Any skipped values can be absorbed into the next retained block; taking the earliest feasible endpoint leaves maximal room for later blocks.

tests.explanation: Keeping four and compressing through each later five yields a non-decreasing array of length three.
The array is already non-decreasing, so all three positions remain.
